newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close with solid gains.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close with solid gains.

text.p: Gains quickened on the Argentine bolsa Thursday reflecting continued strength on the New York markets, dealers said.
"The bolsa continues to have decent volume and is encouraged by this week's stable U.S. long bond yields, although we still can't envisage a rally," said Adolfo Adorno at brokers Roberto Agra y Cia.
The blue-chip MerVal index advanced 1.1 percent to 742.51, extending gains so far this week to 2.6 percent.
"The big question still is: what will the U.S. Federal Reserve do Tuesday?," Adorno said.

"If it hikes rates the measure would be strictly pre-emptive, because this week's U.S inflation data doesn't justify it," he said. "However, a rate hike might be just what the doctor ordered, because the markets would decide it was the last this year and finally relax."
Another trader noted the bolsa now stands practically at an eight-week high, "and if Wall Street stays strong near-term it could test resistance at this year's high of 760."
Floor volume eased to 25.5 million pesos from 27.8 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter deals totaled 118.3 million against 126 million Wednesday.
The broad market index closed up 0.7 percent, with winners smashing losers 40 to 11 and 18 issues closing flat.

Top main-tier performers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which surged 8.9 percent, construction stock Juan Minetti, up 3.5 percent, and steelmaker Acindar and footwear and textile firm Alpargatas, both up 2.9 percent.
MerVal losers were led by carmaker Ciadea, gas distribution company Transportadora de Gas del Sur and foods giant Molinos, which fell 5.1 percent, 1.2 percent and 0.5 percent, respectively.
